title: Stimulation of superconductivity in $d$-wave superconductors
abstract: We study the stimulation of superconductivity by an external electromagnetic radiation --- the Eliashberg effect --- in a disordered $d$-wave superconductor. We use the self-consistent Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical formalism augmented by an inelastic relaxation term to compute the static correction to the pairing amplitude by treating elastic scattering within the Born approximation with the full second-order impurity vertex retained. We find that the clean $d$-wave superconductor shows no enhancement at any frequency: without a momentum relaxation channel a spatially uniform drive produces no absorption, only pair breaking. Elastic impurity scattering restores absorption and with it activates response in the Eliashberg channel. We find enhancement of the pairing amplitude which is confined to a bounded window in frequency, disorder strength, inelastic scattering rate and gap magnitude. Both edges of the window scale with the gap but are set by the competition between quasiparticle redistribution, heating and pair breaking rather than by a feature of the spectrum. Furthermore, in contrast to the $s$-wave when the threshold is pinned at $2Δ$, the upper edge is not pinned to the maximum gap and crosses it as the system approaches the critical temperature.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the Eliashberg effect—the stimulation of superconductivity—in disordered $d$-wave superconductors using advanced Keldysh formalism. The key finding is that the enhancement of the superconducting gap is highly dependent on disorder and inelastic scattering, and crucially, the upper frequency bound does not remain pinned at $2\Delta$ as in $s$-wave materials. This offers a refined theoretical understanding of light-induced superconductivity in unconventional superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates how external electromagnetic radiation (the Eliashberg effect) stimulates or modifies superconductivity in $d$-wave superconductors.
main_result: The enhancement of the pairing amplitude is found to be confined to a bounded frequency window, and unlike $s$-wave superconductors, the upper edge crosses the maximum gap as the system approaches the critical temperature.
method: The authors employ the self-consistent Keldysh–Nambu quasiclassical formalism, augmented by inelastic relaxation terms, to calculate the static, second-order correction to the pairing amplitude.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a disordered $d$-wave superconductor, analyzed using a one-band model of 2D fermions with a $d$-wave attractive interaction in the Cooper channel.
key_observables: Static correction to the pairing amplitude ($\delta\Delta$), superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), and the frequency ($\omega$) dependence of the enhancement.
important_parameters: Elastic scattering rate ($\gamma_{	ext{el}}$), inelastic scattering rate ($\gamma_{	ext{in}}$), and the ratio $\omega/\Delta(T)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the inelastic scattering rate is much smaller than the driving frequency ($\gamma_{	ext{in}} \ll \omega$), and it focuses on the static, second-order shift under a continuous monochromatic drive.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates impurity-assisted absorption in both $s$-wave and $d$-wave systems. Figure 2 shows the equilibrium impurity self-consistency of the $d$-wave state, and Figure 3 shows the temperature dependence of the order parameter.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the theoretical framework using the Keldysh formalism, then calculating the second-order correction to the pairing amplitude ($\delta\Delta$), and finally analyzing the resulting frequency-dependent enhancement window and its temperature dependence.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, non-equilibrium theoretical prediction for how external fields interact with unconventional superconductivity, offering insights into mechanisms beyond simple BCS theory relevant to high-Tc materials.
